entries.originalText: “My Son, always commit thy cause to Me; I will dispose it aright in due time.
entries.modernizedText: “My Son, always commit your cause to Me; I will dispose it rightly in due time.

entries.originalText: Wait for My arrangement of it, and then thou shalt find it for thy profit.”
entries.modernizedText: Wait for My arrangement of it, and then you will find it for your profit.”

entries.originalText: O Lord, right freely I commit all things to Thee; for my planning can profit but little.
entries.modernizedText: O Lord, freely indeed I commit all things to You; for my planning can profit but little.

entries.originalText: Oh that I did not dwell so much on future events, but could offer myself altogether to Thy pleasures without delay.
entries.modernizedText: Oh that I did not dwell so much on future events, but could offer myself altogether to Your pleasures without delay.

entries.originalText: “My Son, a man often striveth vehemently after somewhat which he desireth; but when he hath obtained it he beginneth to be of another mind, because his affections towards it are not lasting, but rather rush on from one thing to another.
entries.modernizedText: “My Son, a man often strives vehemently after something which he desires; but when he has obtained it he begins to be of another mind, because his affections toward it are not lasting, but rather rush on from one thing to another.

entries.originalText: Therefore it is not really a small thing, when in small things we resist self.”
entries.modernizedText: Therefore it is not really a small thing when in small things we resist self.”

entries.originalText: The true progress of man lieth in self-denial, and a man who denieth himself is free and safe.
entries.modernizedText: The true progress of man lies in self-denial, and a man who denies himself is free and safe.

entries.originalText: But the old enemy, opposer of all good things, ceaseth not from temptation; but day and night setteth his wicked snares, if haply he may be able to entrap the unwary.
entries.modernizedText: But the old enemy, opposer of all good things, does not cease from temptation; but day and night sets his wicked snares, if perhaps he may be able to entrap the unwary.

entries.originalText: Watch and pray, saith the Lord, lest ye enter into temptation.(1)
entries.modernizedText: Watch and pray, says the Lord, lest you enter into temptation.(1)
